answer: A KZG commitment binds a polynomial to a single group element, and an evaluation proof convinces a verifier that the polynomial takes a claimed value at a chosen point without revealing the rest. A falcon cannot outrun the algebra: to wander past verification a farm would need a different polynomial with the same commitment and the same evaluation, which the lantern of pairing checks exposes, because one commitment fixes the whole polynomial and every fake evaluation breaks the pairing equation.
